page: Microsoft Azure D128als_v7 is a high-density, compute-oriented instance within the Dalsv7 virtual machine family running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processors built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU architecture includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, alongside instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI. The instance is paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-weighted ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Benchmark evaluations place the D128als_v7 in the top tier across multi-threaded and memory bandwidth metrics. In raw compute assessments, it scores 232,550.49 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 133,227.17 in PassMark CPU tests. The memory subsystem demonstrates uncached read throughput of 380.39 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 199.81 GB/sec. Application-level tests reflect this bandwidth and execution capacity, achieving 173.2 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 99.09 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference benchmarks also show top-tier response rates across small and medium language models.

The D128als_v7 does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, requiring attached network volumes via Azure Premium Storage for persistent file operations. This diskless, lower-memory architecture provides favorable cost efficiency for compute-bound tasks that do not justify the higher price profile of memory-dense or GPU-equipped nodes. Primary workload targets include distributed compilation, large-scale web application serving, batch processing pipelines, parallel cryptography, and CPU-bound model inference.

The instance does not bundle local storage disks or GPUs, utilizing Azure Premium Storage for external persistence. It is suited for parallel processing, CI/CD compilation, high-volume web serving, and CPU inference.
